limits: Tests establish the specified 37-case gate, not a speedup.

findings: The copied baseline has no large observed host discrepancy: median differences from installed are below0.26% in this run. This is descriptive, not a statistical equivalence test.
Direct output has no consistently favorable host direction across the three cases; no stable host speedup established.
Copy-section host time decreases while the chunk interval increases; that interval also contains direct-output view/argument preparation, so this is not proof the FLA GPU kernels became slower.
timing_limits: Host is unsynchronized CPU dispatch latency after each restored pool is synchronized. Each variant uses a seeded random order per iteration.
CUDA-event span includes GPU idle gaps and event enqueue gaps. Near equality with host suggests host-launch limitation but is not an absolute causal diagnosis.
kernel_us is a separate CUDA-profiler device-time difference after subtracting another restore-only pass; it is not an exact uninstrumented kernel measurement and may include device copies.
Per-section measurements are separate sequential passes, not the main no-laps samples. Their medians cannot be added into a median total.
Only medians/p90 are saved, not iteration samples; no confidence interval or paired significance is recoverable.
host median times30 is a serial one-layer extrapolation, not measured service latency or throughput gain.

provenance.external_runner_revision_review: After baseline_laps, external supervisor added BLOCK_NEXT existence checks in its 1s startup/client polls and automatic original-summary export after cleanup. Archived prior runner hash verified; user benchmark/probe/server computation unchanged.

limits: Original user summarize_probe outputs are unchanged. Independent summaries additionally require complete30-call scopes and validate flushed post-main records.
Each control was run once. Do not claim stable speedup, statistical equivalence, or zero probe overhead.
Common-shape comparison uses the intersection of(num_prefills,prefill_tokens,decode_tokens) across all three probe controls. Sparse cells are retained with counts, not treated as significant.
Equal shape is not a pairing of identical requests, random outputs, expert routing or thermal conditions.
sum/span is computed per step then summarized. Span covers the host interval from first to last GDN call, not a complete mixed step and not GPU time.
Host measurements include launch-side blocking when present; host≈GPU event span alone is not definitive causality.
End-to-end throughput includes long generated audio. No audio was saved, so this experiment supplies no WER/SIM comparison.

interpretation: Correctness gate passed unchanged after user slot0 fixture correction.
Copied baseline median host overhead versus installed in the microbenchmark is0.034%,0.250%,0.111%; no large discrepancy observed, not an equivalence proof.
No stable net host gain established: service p50 moves down while mean moves up, and micro host changes are small and not uniformly favorable.
Copy-section time decreases but the chunk interval increases; that interval includes direct-output view/argument setup. This is not a claim that FLA GPU kernels slowed.
The installed and direct service runs have50%/57.14% thermal samples, unlike baseline/no-laps0%; end-to-end differences cannot be attributed to instrumentation or direct output.
Common-shape comparison covers70 shapes but57 have at least one group with fewer than3 samples. Counts and per-shape results are provided without a significance claim.
GDNsum/span is per-step host accounting between first and last GDN calls; it is not whole-step or GPU occupancy.
